title: Analyzer Types & Mapping — review
intro: Task-based walkthrough of the Analyzer Types & Mapping work. Sign in as admin / adminADMIN! first. Mark each step Pass/Fail/N-A and leave a note where anything is confusing or wrong.

steps.do: Sign in with admin / adminADMIN!, then open the Analyzers page.
steps.expect: The analyzers list loads with stat tiles (total / active / inactive) and 9 seeded analyzers (GeneXpert ASTM, Mindray BC-5380 & BS-200 HL7, and several FILE analyzers).

steps.do: Use the search box and the status filter.
steps.expect: The table narrows to matching analyzers; clearing the filter restores the full list; the URL updates so a filtered view is shareable.

steps.do: Click 'Add analyzer' and step through the setup form.
steps.expect: An inline setup form opens (not a dead-end route); required fields are validated; you can pick a type, connection details, and test units.

steps.do: Save the new analyzer, then confirm it appears in the list.
steps.expect: A success confirmation shows and the new analyzer is in the table with the status you set.

steps.do: Open an analyzer's Field Mappings (row action → Field mappings) and review the result-value mapping table.
steps.expect: You can map an instrument code/target to a test and its result; a mapping can target a component of a test; resolution is by stable code, not a display string.

steps.do: Try the Copy mappings action from one analyzer to another of the same type.
steps.expect: Mappings copy across; the target analyzer shows the copied rows; no silent overwrite of unrelated config.

steps.do: Open an analyzer's QC rules page (row action → QC rules).
steps.expect: The QC rule builder loads for that analyzer and lets you define/verify rules.

steps.do: Reflect on the end-to-end flow: could a lab tech set up a new instrument and map its results without developer help?
steps.expect: The guided path (verify deterministic matches, edit only exceptions) feels achievable for a non-developer.
